A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 15 pages of each version, including supplementary sections, equations, tables, figures, and references, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and point-cloud evaluations in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative initialization and failure-case evidence.

M1.justification: The stated photometric predictor in Eq. (7) changes from -∇C·v/||v|| to -∇log(C)·v Δt, revising the prediction used in the photometric losses. This is a localized formulation change within the retained two-branch method; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate EDS, TUM-VIE, and the Robust E-NeRF synthetic dataset for reconstruction and geometry. The added examples remain within existing coverage; flickering illumination was already represented and discussed in v1.

E2.justification: The view-synthesis comparators remain E2VID + 3DGS, Robust E-NeRF, IncEventGS, and EventSplat, with the same participation in corresponding comparisons. Point-cloud comparisons retain E2VID + VGGT and EMVS. v2 Figure 9 visualizes the event-frame initialization alternative already compared qualitatively in v1 Section 3.6.

E3.justification: Reported resolutions, evaluation metrics, gamma correction, event counts of 125k or 500k, and 10k initialization/40k total training steps remain unchanged. Section 8.5 clarifies the existing initialization procedure rather than reporting a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds a visual comparison of IWE-based versus event-frame initialization in Figure 9 and a concrete flicker failure example in Figure 10. These provide additional evidence for previously discussed issues. Existing temporal-window, loss, initialization, sensitivity, runtime, and geometry analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Scene averages and point-estimate reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes Robust E-NeRF's average synthetic PSNR from 28.190 to 26.766, matching its unchanged per-scene values. EventSplat's retained 28.140 consequently becomes the highest reported average. Other numerical results are retained, while Figures 9 and 10 add qualitative initialization and flicker outcomes.

T1.justification: Eq. (7) revises the mathematical brightness prediction to a temporal log-intensity increment and its optical-flow approximation. Section 8.2 additionally spells out the standard matrices underlying the existing motion-field equation; it does not introduce a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds an explicit target-use statement concerning modern monochrome cameras with VGA or higher resolution. The central claims about rendering once, avoiding pretrained priors, real-world reconstruction performance, and temporal-window robustness remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 8.7 makes explicit that flicker generates events away from object edges, producing noisy or blurred reconstruction. The conclusion also clarifies the intended sensor population. Existing static-scene, flicker, and color-Bayer limitations remain otherwise unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with repository access information. Section 8.5 explicitly documents starting with 100k random Gaussians and using rendered C(x) directly during initialization instead of the brightness-change prediction. These clarify the existing procedure and retained training budget.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations on variational contrast-maximization motion segmentation and simultaneous motion/noise estimation. It removes the separate Event collapse in contrast maximization frameworks reference, citing an already included geometric-regularization paper instead. The substantive positioning against prior reconstruction methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 introduces the GPERT name, updates publication, affiliation, and acknowledgment text, and expands the supplementary structure with motion-field, initialization, and failure-case subsections. Most main-text prose and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with clearer rendering branches and the revised photometric expression. Two compact supplementary figures are added, Tables 2 and 4 gain best-value highlighting, and Tables 3 and 5 are relocated. Existing reconstruction and point-cloud figures are retained with resizing or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves consistency by aligning Eq. (7) with the stated log-intensity event model and correcting Table 2's baseline average. Clearer initialization instructions, repository information, and added initialization and failure illustrations improve reproducibility and transparency. These are focused gains; the PDFs do not establish reruns following the formula revision, and the principal experimental evidence remains unchanged.
